name: A Dublin garden

place_source.title: Wikidata: Dublin (Q1761), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A Dublin front garden behind a red-brick terrace: a lawn, a mixed border, hawthorn and Leyland cypress along the fences, an apple tree and a strawberry tree, with magpies, wood pigeons, collared doves and robins by day and foxes and hedgehogs after dark.

facts.text: Dublin has a maritime climate (Köppen Cfb) with mild-warm summers, cool winters and little temperature extremes.

facts.text: Dublin's sheltered location on the east coast makes it the driest place in Ireland, receiving only about half the rainfall of the west coast; the city centre averages 726 mm a year.

source.title: Wikipedia: Dublin

facts.text: At Merrion Square the coldest month is February, with an average minimum temperature of 4.1 °C, and the warmest is July, with an average maximum of 20.1 °C.

source.title: Wikipedia: Dublin

facts.text: The magpie's range runs from Ireland in the west to the Kamchatka Peninsula in the east, and it sometimes breeds at high densities in suburban areas such as parks and gardens.

source.title: Wikipedia: Eurasian magpie
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Eurasian magpie", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The European hedgehog is native to Europe westwards into Ireland, and is most abundant within the gardens, parks and amenity land close to or within human settlements.

source.title: Wikipedia: European hedgehog

facts.text: Grey squirrels were introduced to Ireland by the turn of the 20th century in a single introduction, in County Longford, and control schemes now run in Ireland to favour the native red squirrel.
